✓ Metro-North Railroad.fact: The system took its current form in 1983, when the MTA took over direct operation of Conrail's commuter services in the northern portion of the Tri-State Area and formed Metro-North to run them. There are 124 stations on Metro-North Railroad's five active lines and three branches, which operate on more than 787 miles (1,267 km) of track, with the passenger railroad system totaling 385 miles (620 km) of route.

✓ Metro-North Railroad.question: Supervisors of some towns north of _____ began expressing interest in extending rail service in 2007
✓ Metro-North Railroad.fact: Supervisors of some towns north of Poughkeepsie began expressing interest in extending rail service in 2007. On October 20, 2025, it was announced by Governor Kathy Hochul that Metro-North service on the Hudson line will be extended north from Poughkeepsie to Albany–Rensselaer in 2026.

✓ Metro-North Railroad.question: A groundbreaking ceremony for _____ took place in the Bronx on December 9, 2022
✓ Metro-North Railroad.fact: On October 28, 2015, the MTA Board of Directors approved a 2015–2019 Capital Program which included $695 million in planned spending for the Penn Station Access project. A groundbreaking ceremony for Penn Station Access took place in the Bronx on December 9, 2022.
